operations.name: Judson Simpson

expected.name: Judson Simpson
expected.description: Judson Simpson was a Black sharecropper and Share Croppers' Union member wounded and arrested in the 19 December 1932 Reeltown, Alabama shootout, one of the survivors tried at Dadeville before Judge W. B. Bowling in 1933 and sentenced to 10 to 12 years for "assault with intent to murder." (Ned Cobb was later the subject of Theodore Rosengarten's oral history "All God's Dangers.") On 19 December 1932 a sheriff's posse attacked members of the Communist-led Share Croppers' Union near Reeltown in Tallapoosa County, Alabama, when they resisted the seizure of a member's livestock for debt. Several croppers were shot; the survivors were charged with "assault with intent to murder" and held for the grand jury at the Dadeville jail under $750 bail. The case, following the 1931 Camp Hill affair, became a major ILD Southern defense.

operations.research_note: May19,1933 Daily Worker printedpage2, Bullets Removed from Sharecroppers Jailed for Past Five Months, by Sender Garlin, reports Judson age49 and ten-to-twelve-year sentence; identity tied directly to Tallapoosa trial. Derived circa1884 under authorized age-based birthyear workflow. Exact birthyear could be1883 or1884; no exact birthday claimed. Original scan visually inspected.

operations.name: Charles Coder

expected.name: Charles Coder
expected.description: Charles Coder was a white co-leader of the Dallas unemployment movement in Dallas, Texas in 1931; after a demonstration of four thousand for unemployment insurance, he was jailed and then handed over to the Ku Klux Klan, flogged, and left for dead before being rescued by Black farmers.

operations.research_note: March13,1931 Daily Worker identifies Dallas TUUL organizer Charles Coder as30. Derived circa1901 under authorized age-based birthyear workflow; actual year could be1900or1901. No exactbirthday claimed. Contemporary reports initially falsely presumed death; do not add death date. Subsequent March21 Southern Worker confirms survival. No exact arrest date inferred from demonstration date.
